calls.reason: The forecast explicitly expresses uncertainty about a fix arriving soon. Magesh finds persistent legal hallucinations, while Farquhar shows partial detection progress; neither settles the loosely timed claim.
The Decoder reports losses for 2022, leaving profitability at publication unclear. Google’s results and the LMSYS rankings show competition but do not establish whether OpenAI had a durable moat.

IBM’s November survey found 42% exploring generative AI, while O’Reilly reported only 18% with production applications. Together they support the ordinary reading that many companies were still experimenting.

OpenAI’s parliamentary submission explicitly lists licensed material among its training sources. AP confirms an actual agreement, but licensing’s availability does not support Marcus’s central accusation that OpenAI presented free access as the only option.

Kabir’s programming study found mixed accuracy and users overlooking plausible errors. Dahl’s legal study also found frequent hallucinations and unreliable self-assessment, supporting the difficulty of recognizing false answers.

The News Corp agreement confirms licensing, and the court order confirms ongoing litigation. Neither provides payout amounts or a profit comparison showing that these costs cut heavily into potential earnings.
